research_page.title: The Centiloid Project: Standardizing Quantitative Amyloid Plaque Estimation by PET
research_page.description: Introduces a standardized 0-100 scale (Centiloids) for amyloid PET imaging to enable direct comparison across different tracers and centers.
research_page.authors_line_md: Klunk et al. — University of Pittsburgh / Avid Radiopharmaceuticals (Eli Lilly)
research_page.takeaway_md: The Centiloid scale provides a universal 0-100 metric for amyloid PET scans, anchoring 0 to young, healthy brains and 100 to typical Alzheimer's disease. This standard allows clinical trials and researchers to compare plaque clearance directly, regardless of the specific radiotracer or imaging hardware used.
key_findings_md: Anchored a 0-100 scale using young controls (≤45 years) for 0 and typical mild-to-moderate AD patients for 100 (paper, Section 1.3.2).
Identified the whole cerebellum as the optimal standard reference region due to its low signal variance in healthy controls (paper, Section 1.3.1).
Demonstrated that different tracers and analysis methods can be reliably scaled to Centiloids, achieving a 0.991 correlation with standard PiB methods in a validation subset (paper, Section 2.5).
research_page.methods_md: Retrospective methodological study analyzing 125 subjects: 34 young controls (≤45 years), 47 typical mild-to-moderate AD patients, and 44 additional subjects for region-of-interest definition. The project developed a standard Level-1 baseline method using PiB-PET and a Level-2 calibration process for non-standard tracers.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: The Centiloid scale has become the foundational metric for measuring amyloid clearance in modern Phase 3 clinical trials. Pivotal trials like CLARITY AD (lecanemab) and [TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2](/trials/trailblazer-alz-2-nct04437511) have utilized Centiloids not just as secondary endpoints, but to define strict threshold criteria for clinical outcomes and stopping patient dosing (e.g., <11 Centiloids for clearance).
research_page.sentiment_md: The scientific and clinical research communities enthusiastically treat Centiloids as the definitive common language for amyloid quantification. However, this metric remains almost entirely absent from public and patient discourse, where conversations focus firmly on top-line cognitive benefits and drug brand names.
caveats_md: The scale's anchor points were established using cross-sectional data, meaning longitudinal performance across different reference regions requires further validation.

The standardization method does not completely account for variance caused by substantial differences in scanner hardware, reconstruction algorithms, or attenuation correction protocols across imaging sites.
Applying Centiloid scaling to small, specific brain regions (like the precuneus) rather than the global cortex can distort the numerical meaning of the 0-100 scale.
relates_to_md: [Biomarkers](/research/biomarkers) — Establishes the universal reporting standard for amyloid PET imaging.
[Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — Provides the exact metric used to quantify amyloid clearance in modern trials.

trial_pages.title: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
trial_pages.description: Phase 3 trial of donanemab in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS)
trial_pages.why_md: A pivotal Phase 3 trial that demonstrated donanemab's efficacy in slowing clinical decline. It notably validated the clinical utility of the [Centiloid scale](/research/papers/centiloid-project-standardization) by using rigid Centiloid thresholds to define amyloid clearance and safely halt patient dosing.
trial_pages.results_md: Phase 3 results confirmed that donanemab significantly slowed clinical progression. The trial successfully utilized Centiloid thresholds (<24.1 and <11) to define amyloid clearance and guide the cessation of patient dosing, directly linking the radiological metric to clinical management.

timeline_entries.title: 2015-01 — Centiloid Project standardizes amyloid PET
timeline_entries.body_md: The [Centiloid Project](/research/papers/centiloid-project-standardization) establishes a universal 0-100 scale for quantifying amyloid plaques, enabling direct comparisons across different imaging tracers and analysis methods.
